subject: Mathematics
central_question: How do limits and derivatives describe smooth local behaviour, and how can advanced differentiation rules and mean value theorems be applied?
in_scope_units: 5.1 Introduction: extension of differentiation from Class XI.
5.2 Continuity: pointwise continuity, interval continuity and algebra of continuous functions.
5.3 Differentiability: definition, left and right derivatives, chain rule and inverse-trigonometric derivatives.
5.6 Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms.
5.8 Mean Value Theorem: Rolle and Lagrange mean value theorems.
banned_topics: Applications of derivatives to maxima and minima

known_pitfalls.claim: A function is continuous whenever its graph can be drawn without lifting the pen.
known_pitfalls.correction: That picture is informal; the precise condition is lim f(x)=f(c) at each domain point, with one-sided limits at endpoints.
Differentiability implies continuity, but a continuous function such as |x| need not be differentiable at 0.

known_pitfalls.claim: Infinity is a real limit value.
Rolle theorem applies whenever endpoint values are equal.
known_pitfalls.correction: Continuity on [a,b] and differentiability on (a,b) are also required.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 3 to prove |x| is continuous at 0.
Use the standard |x| derivative check to show non-differentiability at 0.
Use an inverse-trigonometric derivative exercise for sin inverse x.
Use a parametric derivative example followed by a second derivative example.
Use the Rolle or Lagrange Mean Value Theorem examples from Section 5.8.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 5.1 to 5.8 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 5.
